$comment: Single source of truth for the emulator both a laptop and CI boot. create.sh and create.ps1 read this file and produce the same AVD from it; a CI workflow reads systemImage/device/config to fill in reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner's inputs (see the ci block below) without checking in a second copy of these numbers. Changing any value here is a deliberate re-pin, not a tweak: it invalidates every capture taken against the old AVD as a comparison baseline. See README.md#emulator for why.

systemImage.$comment: packageId is what sdkmanager/avdmanager resolve. Everything else here is not consulted by either tool -- it is recorded so a human (or a CI assertion) can catch the day Google republishes the same packageId with different bits behind it. That has happened to public system images before; a package id survives it, a build id does not.

device.$comment: avdmanager's --device profile. pixel_6 rather than whatever the tool lists as 'latest' -- an implicit default drifts every time a new Pixel profile ships, which is the exact failure mode this ticket exists to close. The profile only supplies defaults; config below overrides the fields that actually affect reproducibility.

config.$comment: Written into the AVD's config.ini after creation, every run, so a laptop AVD created months ago converges to the same values as one created today. Most keys map 1:1 onto config.ini keys; see create.sh/create.ps1 applyConfig. refreshRateHz is the one exception worth flagging: the emulator has no 'hw.lcd.refreshRate' property (that key does not exist in emulator/lib/hardware-properties.ini and is silently ignored if written) -- the real key is 'hw.lcd.vsync'. This is the field mcp/src/report.ts's comparability() gates on, via the runtime's own Display.getRefreshRate() reading, so writing the wrong ini key does not just fail to pin the number, it makes the gate check something that was never actually set. snapshotsEnabled=false is enforced by disabling every snapshot-related knob together (snapshot.present, fastboot.forceColdBoot/forceFastBoot, firstboot.bootFromLocalSnapshot/saveToLocalSnapshot) -- a pinned AVD exists to remove drift, and a boot that can silently resume from a stale snapshot on some knobs while others insist on cold boot is exactly that drift, one level down.

ci.$comment: Handed to GRA-101 (owns .github/workflows/*, not touched here). reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner takes api-level/target/arch, not a packageId, so it cannot pin the build directly the way create.sh/create.ps1 do -- it resolves 'android-35 google_atd x86_64' through sdkmanager same as anyone typing that string would, and Google could republish under that tag. The mitigating step, left for GRA-101 to wire in: after boot, run `adb shell getprop ro.build.version.incremental` and fail the job if it does not equal systemImage.buildIncremental below. That turns an unpinnable input into a detected pin. inputs.profile and inputs.cores are the action's own native inputs and pin device.profile/config.cpuCores directly. inputs.emulator-options carries '-vsync-rate 60' (a real emulator flag -- see `emulator -help-all`) to pin config.refreshRateHz the same way create.sh/create.ps1 do via hw.lcd.vsync. inputs.lcdDensity has no equivalent in this action (no CLI flag, no action input) and cannot be pinned at boot time the same way; it is still recorded here so a cache key built from this whole block reflects the AVD's full identity rather than a partial one, and GRA-101 should apply it post-boot the same way postBootVerification already does for the build pin, e.g. `adb shell wm density 420` (a real, verified WindowManager shell command) followed by re-reading `adb shell wm density` to confirm it took.
